info.name: McLogix 360 FGA Workshop
info.description:
Run the folders in order with the Collection Runner after `npm run setup` and `npm run dev`. Folder 0 resets data so the whole collection is re-runnable. Identity comes from the x-user-id header: DEMO ONLY, never do this in production.

READ THIS FIRST: FGA decides, the API serves the data. The responses in this collection are NOT FGA responses. Auth0 FGA only stores relationships and answers 'is this user allowed?' (allowed: true/false, or a list of ids). It has never heard of item names or quantities. The API layer asks FGA and, only if the answer is yes, returns the order from the application's own database. A 200 with an item and quantity = FGA said yes + data from the database. A 403 = FGA said no, and the API layer returned no order data. A 404 = our database has no such order, so FGA was never asked. The 'fga' array in each response is FGA's side of the conversation, included for the workshop only. See README.md, 'The one idea to take away'.

item.name: 0. Reset & Sync
item.description: Run first. Resets the in-memory DB and replaces ALL tuples with fga/tuples.json. Demo only: this endpoint is unauthenticated and destructive.

exec: pm.test("4 orders and 15 tuples", () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.orders).to.eql(4); pm.expect(d.tuplesWritten).to.eql(15); });

request.description: Resets the DB and re-syncs FGA tuples. No supplierId needed.

item.name: Alice (Sales, Supplier A)
item.description: Sales rep at Supplier A. Can place orders for supplier_a only; sees only orders she placed.

request.description:
listObjects(user:alice, can_view, order). No supplierId needed.

What to notice: FGA's listObjects returned only the id order:1001. The item/quantity rows were looked up in the application database.

Allowed: alice is placed_by order:1001.

What to notice: the item and quantity in this 200 come from the application database. FGA only said allowed: true (see the fga array). Code: app/api/orders/[id]/route.ts, the respond(200, ...) line.

Denied: same supplier, but a different sales rep placed it.

What to notice: FGA said allowed: false. The API layer turned that into a 403 and returned NO order data; the row never leaves the database.

Unknown order returns 404.

What to notice: the 404 comes from the application database. FGA was never asked, so the fga array is empty.
Use supplierId supplier_a (her own supplier). Expect 201.
Use supplierId supplier_b. Alice belongs to supplier_a, so FGA denies. Expect 403.

item.name: DELETE the order she just placed

request.description: Allowed: she placed it. Cleans up so later folders see the seed data.
